start.title: Learn UPI Scams by Practising
start.subtitle: Spot red flags in realistic messages, make the right call under pressure, and see what happens without risking real money.

tips.pin: You never enter a UPI PIN or scan a QR code to receive money.
tips.links: Banks never send links to update KYC or unblock accounts. Always open your official bank app.
tips.arrest: Police, CBI, or courts never arrest anyone on a video call or ask for money to 'verify' accounts.
tips.apps: Never install APK files from links or share your screen on support calls.

customScenario.verifyFeedback: Always check inside your official bank app independently — and when red flags appear, ignoring or reporting on 1930 is safest.
customScenario.defaultFeedback: Review all matched triggers and verify through official channels before acting.
customScenario.rule: Never act on a message that rushes you. Verify in your official app.

verify.title: Verify Before, During & After Payment
verify.subtitle: A heuristic Safety Check & verification assistant to help spot UPI risk before, while, and after you pay—not a guarantee.
verify.demoBanner: DEMO Safety Check (verification assistant): Heuristic check only, not a guarantee. Fictional merchants, no real payments. Always confirm the receiver's name inside your payment app before entering your PIN.

honesty.beforeBody: To RECEIVE money you never need to enter a PIN. A ₹1 'request' that promises ₹10 back is a scam.
honesty.whileBody: The only name you can trust is the one on YOUR payment app's confirmation screen. Match it before entering your UPI PIN — every time.
honesty.afterTitle: If someone is directing you on a call
honesty.afterBody: Screen-sharing apps + phone instructions to pay = digital arrest scam. Stop the payment, hang up, call 1930.

qr.heading: Before you pay: QR & UPI link inspector
qr.sub: Decode a UPI QR or link offline in your browser before opening your payment app.
qr.camUnavailable: Camera unavailable or permission denied. Upload/paste a QR image or paste the upi:// link below instead.
qr.pasteZoneHint: Paste a QR image (Ctrl+V) or drop/choose a PNG/JPG file.
qr.noQrFound: Could not detect a UPI QR code in that image. Try uploading a sharper image or pasting the upi:// link.
qr.invalidUri: Enter or scan a valid upi://pay?... payment link.
qr.registryHeading: Demo Bank (fictional) says this VPA is registered to:
qr.registryMatchNote: Still check your payment app's confirmation screen before entering your UPI PIN.
qr.registryMismatchBadge: Name mismatch warning — do not pay
qr.registryUnknownNote: Not in the demo registry. A real app would call the PSP's name-lookup API here.
qr.registryMissingPn: This QR does not declare a payee name. Extra reason to check your payment app's confirmation screen.
qr.honestCanText: Decode and compare the QR's self-declared fields.
qr.honestCannotText: Confirm the real bank-registered name without PSP/bank rails; the only trusted name is on your payment app's confirmation screen.

tab1.explainer: Check whether a UPI ID matches a registered Demo Bank business or looks like a typo trap before sending money.
tab1.upiRequired: Please enter a UPI ID to check.

verdictDesc.VERIFIED_DEMO: This UPI ID and name match a registered Demo Bank merchant.
verdictDesc.NAME_MISMATCH: This UPI ID is registered to a different business name. Pause and double-check.
verdictDesc.LOOKALIKE: This ID is not registered, and is dangerously close to a real Demo Bank ID (possible typosquatting).
verdictDesc.UNKNOWN: Cannot be verified here — always confirm the merchant's ID in person or via official bills.

tab2.explainer: Generate an HMAC-signed DemoPay link and QR code, then test what happens if anyone alters the amount.
tab2.sealLine: A digital seal that locks amount, receiver and order
tab2.invalidAmount: Enter a valid amount between Rs.0.01 and Rs.100,000.
tab2.tryHint: Change the amount below to simulate an attacker editing the payment link, then tap Check.
tab2.statusValid: Valid digital seal — details match the issuer's signature.
tab2.statusTampered: Signature mismatch: the payment details were changed
tab2.statusExpired: Expired: this signed code passed its 10-minute validity window.

lab.heading: Tamper Lab: Demo Bank signed QR
lab.sub: Create a fictional Demo Bank order, tamper with a field, and watch HMAC verification reject it.
lab.demoBanner: Demo mode — key is public, for offline demonstration only
lab.signedPrefix: Signed by Demo Bank (fictional) · expires in
lab.togglesTitle: Apply tamper simulation (keeps the original signature):
lab.validBody: All fields match the issuer's HMAC-SHA256 signature cleanly.
lab.invalidBody: Payload fields were modified after signing; the payment token is rejected.
lab.expiredBody: Order validity window (5 minutes) has elapsed. Request a fresh QR from the merchant.
lab.honestyBody: In production, signature verification lives inside the PSP/NPCI rails. This demo shows the tamper-evidence principle with a fictional bank.

tab3.explainer: Every confirmed demo payment links to the previous receipt's SHA-256 hash so silent edits break the chain.
tab3.emptyTrail: No demo receipts yet. Tap 'Confirm demo payment' at least twice to build a hash-chained trail.
tab3.needTwoForTamper: Confirm at least 2 demo payments first so entry #2 can be tampered.
tab3.tamperDone: Locally edited amount on entry #2 without updating hashes. Now tap 'Verify trail'.

ev.heading: Transaction receipt & fraud-report prep
ev.sub: Save a local tamper-evident receipt and turn it into a 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in script offline.
ev.rrnLabel: RRN (optional — paste from your UPI app)
ev.notesPlaceholder: What happened or what was promised?
ev.verifyFileSub: Upload or paste a saved receipt .json to check if anything was edited later.
ev.unchangedTitle: UNCHANGED — hash matches the exported receipt
ev.modifiedTitle: MODIFIED — file contents differ from the signed SHA-256 hash
ev.honestBody: Receipts are stored locally on your device. This is evidence preparation, not an official record — always report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in regardless.

limits.title: What this Safety Check can and cannot do
limits.canText: Spots changed amounts, edited receiver/order fields, expired links, and tampered demo receipts in this heuristic verification assistant.
limits.cannotText: Cannot guarantee safety, verify random unsigned QR codes from strangers, or stop you if a scammer tricks you into paying their own valid account willingly.

go.title: Check before you go
go.subtitle: Inspect a link offline in your browser before deciding whether to open it.
go.emptyNote: No destination link found in the URL fragment (#u=...). Paste a link in Check to create a protected link, or test the demo link below.
go.blockedBody: Only standard http:// or https:// links up to 2000 characters are allowed here. Unsafe or malformed links (such as javascript:, data:, file:, or intent:) are stopped automatically.
go.lowSummary: No strong red flags found. Still be careful.

riskSummary.MEDIUM: Suspicious patterns detected. Double-check the bold domain before opening.
riskSummary.HIGH: High risk: multiple deceptive link patterns detected. Going back is strongly recommended.
riskSummary.CRITICAL: Critical risk: strong scam or malicious pattern detected. Do not open unless verified independently.

url.ipAddress: Points to a raw IP address instead of a real bank or company domain.

url.noHttps: Uses unencrypted HTTP instead of HTTPS.
url.keyword: Includes deceptive banking or KYC keywords inside the web address.
url.brandImpersonation: Impersonates a trusted brand using an unofficial domain name.
url.typosquatting: Lookalike spelling mimics an official website.
